coreIdea: Cycle time = max(stage delays)+latch. Total time (n instr, k stages) = (k+n-1)×cycle_time. Speedup→k asymptotically. RAW=data hazard(forwarding), WAR/WAW=renaming, resource conflict=structural.
mustRememberFormulas: Cycle time = max(all stage delays) + latch delay
Non-pipelined total = n × Σ(all stage delays)

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: stage delays given, asked cycle time or total execution time
pipelined vs non-pipelined comparison, or two designs compared
instruction sequence, register overlap, hazard type or forwarding asked
delayed branching, delay slot instruction safety

commonTrapsQuickList: Don't forget the latch delay when computing cycle time
(k+n-1) formula is IDEAL — add extra cycles explicitly for stated stalls/branch penalties
Register renaming solves WAR/WAW, NOT RAW — RAW needs forwarding/stalling
Delay-slot instruction executes UNCONDITIONALLY, regardless of branch outcome
highYieldPyqLessons: Timing computation (18/39) is the single biggest sub-skill in all of CO&A after Cache Memory — the formulas are simple, practice until automatic.
Hazard classification (11/39) rewards knowing the RAW/WAR/WAW distinction cold, plus matching each to its correct resolution technique.
